subject: Clarifying per-tenant retention carveouts — Keystone Therapeutics (SOC 2 / CAIQ evidence)
messages:
From: Amy Lee <amy.lee@keystonetx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Paul Ramirez <paul.ramirez@keystonetx.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant-specific retention carveouts / SOC2 evidence ask

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — Keystone is moving through procurement and we hit one technical gating item from InfoSec. Our compliance team needs a short write-up and evidence showing how Redwood would handle a customer-level retention carveout: specifically, we need to understand the operational process and artifacts for a tenant-specific extension to session/log TTLs (we may request a 180-day extension for debugging traces tied to a regulated trial).

Requested deliverables:
- Short description of the policy and approval path for per-tenant retention carveouts (who approves, what controls are applied)
- Evidence artifacts you can provide (SOC 2 control mappings, CAIQ snapshot answers, exportability of logs, proof-of-delete workflow)
- Any limiting controls (e.g., scoped keystore residency, masking, sampling) and estimated timeline to stand up a carveout

We don't need legal terms yet — this is an InfoSec intake. Can you route to the right person and share what you can in the next 48 hours?

Appreciate it,
Amy
Amy Lee
Head of Security & Compliance
Keystone Therapeutics

Attachments: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lee <amy.lee@keystonetx.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant-specific retention carveouts / SOC2 evidence ask

Amy — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Olga (Product Security) and Neha (Compliance) to provide the artifacts and the operational description. Quick notes up front so expectations are aligned:

- Redwood supports per-tenant retention carveouts as an operational control rather than a product flag; carveouts are recorded in our Ticketing & Change system and require an approval from Product Security + Compliance for anything beyond 90 days.
- Typical controls for extensions: scoped access roles, masking of PII at rest, scoped-keystore (if required), and time-boxed sampling for debug traces.
- Evidence we can provide immediately: SOC 2 control references mapping to retention (we'll point to relevant CC8/CC6 controls in our SOC2 report), a CAIQ snapshot exported for your account, and a sample retention matrix that shows the operational steps and rollback. For proof-of-delete we can provide the deletion job run logs and manifest (redacted as needed).

What we'll deliver by EOD tomorrow: a one-page operational description, a CAIQ snapshot (export), and a draft retention matrix for Keystone showing proposed 180-day handling and compensating controls. If you need cryptographic keystore residency guarantees (customer-managed KMS/HSM), that adds a short procurement step.

Olga / Neha — can one of you own the one-pager + CAIQ snapshot? Olga, if you can include the mitigation checklist (RBAC, sampling, masking) that'd be great. Neha, please add the SOC 2 control references and any customer-facing attestation language. I'll assemble and send to Amy.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Lee <amy.lee@keystonetx.com>, Paul Ramirez <paul.ramirez@keystonetx.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant-specific retention carveouts / SOC2 evidence ask

Karthik — sending the first-pass artifacts per your ask. See attachments and the CAIQ link below. High-level summary included for Amy so InfoSec can triage quickly.

--- Begin summary ---
Operational flow (short):
1) Customer requests carveout (ticket created, change-id CHG-7482).
2) Product Security reviews risk and required compensating controls.
3) Compliance signs off for auditability requirements.
4) Engineering schedules time-boxed retention change scoped to tenant IDs; change is implemented in a gated rollout with monitoring and automated rollback.

Controls applied for Keystone 180d request:
- RBAC: limit access to a named debug team; audit trails enabled at token level.
- Masking: default PII redaction for fields with PHI/PII before storage in persistent traces.
- Scoped-keystore: option to require customer-managed KMS for TTL extension if Keystone requests full custody.
- Sampling & rotation: sample rate for long-lived traces to limit volume; nightly prune jobs run to ensure non-customer data is not retained.

Artifacts attached/shared:
- keystone_caiq_snapshot_20260517.pdf (CAIQ answers scoped to the Keystone request)
- keystone_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx (proposed operational steps, roles, and evidence artifacts)
- Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/keystone/caiq-answers-2026-05-17

Proof-of-delete: We can produce deletion manifests and the job run logs (sha256 of manifest) for customer-scoped retention deletes. If Keystone needs signed attestations, Compliance can prepare a templated attestation for carveouts.

Questions for Keystone: Is the 180-day ask for all traces or limited to specific trace types (debug-only vs session transcripts)? Also, do you require customer-managed KMS?

--- End summary ---

Amy / Paul — attaching the files now. If InfoSec wants a short call to walk through the matrix I'm available this week Wednesday/Thursday.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: keystone_caiq_snapshot_20260517.pdf; keystone_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lee <amy.lee@keystonetx.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant-specific retention carveouts / SOC2 evidence ask

Amy — following up on Olga's packet. A couple of compliance clarifications and next steps:

- SOC 2: The controls that map to retention and deletion are documented in section CC6/CC8 of our SOC 2 Type II. For customer carveouts we provide a scoped SOC2 attest mapping and can add a short paragraph to the SOC 2 bridge letter describing that carveouts are an approved operational exception with compensating controls.
- Evidence bundle: the CAIQ snapshot contains our configuration answers; the retention matrix shows the ticket/change ids and what artifacts we will hand over during an audit (deletion manifests, job logs, signed attestation).
- Timeline: We can deliver a signed attestation and the final retention matrix by EOD Thursday (2026-05-21) provided Keystone confirms which trace types are in-scope.

Requested action from Keystone: please confirm scope ("debug traces only" or "all session logs") and whether you require a customer-managed KMS for extended retention. Once we have that we will lock down the final artifacts and a date for the attestation.

If a short intake call helps, Karthik / Olga and I can join a 30-min call Wed 10–11am PT.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
